survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note synthesises indicator results from Education at a Glance 2025 rather than estimating a student-level model in the note itself. The note reports cross-country comparisons for outcomes such as tertiary attainment, unemployment by educational attainment, and adult literacy proficiency from the OECD Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC), but it does not describe an analytic subsample or the application of complex survey weights within this document. For users who replicate the underlying indicators, the relevant OECD/PIAAC and Education at a Glance technical documentation should be consulted for the specific sampling design, scaling, and weighting procedures used to produce the published estimates. Because no student-level microdata analysis is conducted here, the note does not specify weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) at the country-note level.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD country note that reports published indicator statistics (e.g., shares, gaps, and literacy score differences) rather than conducting an original student-level predictive/achievement analysis with PV-based outcomes. Plausible values and missing-data handling are therefore not applicable to the note’s own methods; they are handled upstream in the Education at a Glance 2025 indicator production process. Missing-data handling is not reported in this country note because it does not present an original estimation pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the latest available indicator data for Israel as published in Education at a Glance 2025; the note does not define an analytic student-level subsample or inclusion/exclusion criteria.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Israel summarises key characteristics of the education system using the latest available indicator data. It highlights intergenerational educational inequality in tertiary attainment (e.g., a 38 percentage-point gap in tertiary attainment among 25–34 year-olds by parental education), unemployment differences by educational attainment, and adult literacy proficiency from the OECD Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC), including literacy-level shares and literacy-score gaps between attainment groups. The note also reports trends in adult literacy between PIAAC Cycle 1 (2012–15) and Cycle 2 (2023), participation in education and training by literacy level, and several tertiary education access and progression indicators (e.g., entry pathways, gap years, completion rates, and international student mobility). Because it is a descriptive synthesis of published indicators rather than an original ML/PV-based analysis, no model performance metrics, PV handling, or missing-data procedures are specified within the note.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The document is not an empirical ML study and does not report an original student-level dataset, analytic sample size, or predictive modeling results. It is a descriptive country note that aggregates indicator outputs from Education at a Glance 2025 and related OECD surveys (notably PIAAC), so fields required for ML extraction (e.g., PV handling in an estimation pipeline, missing-data strategy, and model metrics) are not applicable at this level of reporting.
